purpose: Separate D cell identity from fourth-process accumulated state and test whether a fresh per-process IPC namespace with runtime-owned Carbonite teardown changes the table-USD-to-PhysX boot boundary.

probe_scope.success_marker: first Physics using context line after exact table USD load

decision_rules.ordinal_supported: At both namespace levels D-first reaches PhysX while ordinal-4 fails at the frozen boundary.
decision_rules.namespace_cleanup_supported: At the same ordinal host-IPC fails while private-IPC reaches PhysX, with all other bound inputs equal.
decision_rules.interaction_supported: Only ordinal-4 host-IPC fails while ordinal-4 private-IPC reaches PhysX and both D-first cells reach PhysX.
decision_rules.cell_identity_supported: D fails as first process in both namespace levels while A/B/C exact scene probes reach PhysX under matched inputs.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Any source, asset, scene, supervisor, probe-order, capacity or receipt mismatch; or any outcome not uniquely classified by the rules above.

prerequisites_before_execution_review: Materialize a reviewed scene-boot-only harness that exits immediately after the first PhysX context marker.
Bind exact source, Python, Isaac/Kit runtime, A3 asset tree, table USD and scene configuration bytes.
Use separate fresh container or equivalent identical base snapshot for each factorial cell.
Prove private IPC cleanup is namespace teardown only and cannot unlink host or another process's shared memory.
Use reviewed exact-PGID or pidfd supervision with no broad kill path.
Predeclare no-clobber paths and preserve every timeout log before any later cell.
Obtain a separate explicit execution approval after source and static tests are reviewed.
